title: Session burst cap & directional IO smoothing experiment
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Pilot an ingress/egress-aware per-session burst cap and directional IO smoothing policy for the Hosted API. Goal is to reduce billing disputes from enterprise customers hitting asymmetric streaming workloads, prevent per-session runaway costs, and explore a session-scoped soft floor that adapts to observed input/output ratios. This ticket covers specification, telemetry requirements, A/B design, billing simulation, and contract questionnaire alignment for enterprise SQs.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ava: Kickoff doc linked; purpose is to limit upside billing spikes for sessions with heavy output while preserving burst UX for chat-heavy customers. Asking Eng for feasibility of per-session stateful counters in the gateway.

2026-02-18 - Liam: Eng assessment: gateway can maintain 60s sliding window token counters per session using existing KV prefix with negligible p50 latency impact. Need to add metric tags for session_id and direction (ingress/egress) for billing pipeline and metrics ingestion.

2026-02-28 - Design feedback (Maya Patel): Recommend UX hinting in SDK / Console so customers know when session burst cap applied and where to request waivers; add a webhook event for 'session_burst_throttled' for observability.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature flag toggles per-account rollout and can be disabled globally. 2) Session-level counters exposed in Console and via audit logs; webhook emitted for throttle events. 3) Billing simulation shows less than 1% revenue deviation in baseline cohorts and customer dispute rate drops in A/B test. 4) SDK/Console UX includes explanatory copy and opt-in pathway for legacy contracts. 5) Legal sign-off for enterprise contract language is recorded.
experiment_design: Randomized A/B at account level for 6 weeks: 20% treatment accounts (apply per-session burst cap and directional smoothing), 80% control. Treatment parameters start at 5k token/session burst cap with directional smoothing factor that shifts excess egress into a separate adaptive floor credit pool. Monitor KPIs daily; data-science to run uplift analysis after 3 and 6 weeks. Include a small enterprise holdout group for targeted sales outreach.
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback (disable flag) if session_throttle_rate > 2% for top 500 accounts, or p95 gateway latency increases by >10ms after rollout, or spike in billing disputes >25% relative to control.
notes: Trade-offs: tighter burst caps reduce revenue variance but may frustrate long-form generation customers; directional smoothing helps preserve UX for low-input-high-output flows (e.g., summarization) but adds billing complexity. We'll pair with clear billing transparency in Console and an opt-in waiver workflow for enterprise contracts. Plan to revisit thresholds after the first week of live traffic.
implementation_steps: Spec complete and sign-off from Legal/Design/DataScience
Add session counter in gateway and event webhook
Implement billing adapter to apply session caps and adaptive floor credits
Create feature flag and rollout plan per account tier
Run load tests and staging validation
